page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the n4 family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel x86_64 cores with 2 threads per core, utilizing a dedicated CPU allocation. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The underlying Intel processor features a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware support for Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations.

Benchmark results indicate that the n4-highmem-8 delivers average performance across most compute and memory workloads. In CPU-bound tests, it achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1815.0 and a multi-core score of 6984.0, while the Passmark CPU score stands at 13039.39. Memory performance is characterized by a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 542.3 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 37.24 GB/sec. For database and key-value store operations, the instance handles 9.89 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 4891.5 on Passmark database operations. However, multi-threaded decompression tasks show relative weakness, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the bottom 25% at 36.86 GB/sec. Additionally, while small-model LLM inference is average, text generation with a medium 7B model is poor, yielding only 6.1 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-highmem-8 offers a high resource density of memory relative to its compute footprint, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing power. The presence of AMX and AVX-512 instruction sets provides hardware-level acceleration for cryptography and integer operations without requiring dedicated GPU hardware. This instance is suitable for workloads such as database caching, in-memory data processing, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference on small models.
